prompt: Write the ORDER BY clause: highest total_lag first (descending), and when two groups tie, group c.group_id alphabetically (ascending). Name both sort keys with their own direction, separated by a comma.
given: Query: SELECT c.group_id, SUM(...) AS total_lag FROM ... GROUP BY c.group_id HAVING ... <your clause>
template:
-- EXPECTED: [["billing", 60], ["zeta", 60], ["fraud", 50], ["analytics", 40]]

-- Tables are loaded for you: partitions(topic, partition_id, log_end_offset) and commits(group_id, topic, partition_id, committed_offset).
SELECT c.group_id,
       SUM(p.log_end_offset - c.committed_offset) AS total_lag
FROM commits c
JOIN partitions p ON p.topic = c.topic AND p.partition_id = c.partition_id
GROUP BY c.group_id
HAVING SUM(p.log_end_offset - c.committed_offset) > 0
@@BLANK@@
;
answer: ORDER BY total_lag DESC, c.group_id ASC
why: ORDER BY takes multiple keys separated by commas, each with its own direction. The second key breaks ties.
